title: Add VPC control plane provisioning: subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, Route53 (terraform + private-installer)
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: enable the Private deployment installer and Terraform modules to fully provision a VPC-hosted control plane with opinionated defaults for subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 private hosted zones. This PR closes gaps customers hit during Private deployments where manual network work was required and it integrates upgrade/rollback hooks used by the private-installer to support smoother upgrades.

What this changes: consolidated Terraform modules under modules/vpc-control-plane that create (configurable) multi-AZ private subnets, AWS interface endpoints (S3, STS, EC2, ECR, KMS), security group templates for control-plane components, cross-account VPC peering resources with automatic route propagation, and Route53 private hosted zone + records for control-plane discovery. The private-installer package is updated to call the modules and now emits a stable network manifest used by the installer and the Helm chart for logical mapping. Upgrade and rollback hooks were added to the installer to detect and revert a failed networking step without leaving dangling peering or route table entries.

Key design notes: - Opinionated defaults for CIDR allocation to avoid overlap with typical customer ranges; explicitly configurable overrides. - All resources tagged with managed_by=redwood and cluster_id to assist cleanup. - Endpoint policies are permissive enough for control-plane operations but scoped to the control-plane SG. - Peering includes an idempotent lookup + create flow to support re-runs. - Route53 records created for internal control-plane DNS (controlplane.<cluster>.local) and kept in a private hosted zone provisioned per-account or shared via delegation depending on input variables.

Checklist: [x] Terraform modules complete and exported [x] private-installer wiring and network manifest generation [x] Helm chart values mapping (examples) [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks implemented [x] Integration tests in perf-canary run (local sim) [x] Docs updated (redwood-docs/networking)

Testing performed: unit tests for TF modules using terraform-compliance and terratest mocks; end-to-end validation in internal staging account (staging-net-03) with canary private-installer run, verifying: subnet creation, endpoints reachable from control-plane EC2 (bastion check), peering established and routes programmed, Route53 records resolvable inside peered VPC. CI runs include terraform fmt/lint, plan validation, unit tests for installer scripts, and Helm chart linting.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: the installer will detect an existing control-plane manifest and perform in-place updates where possible. A migration path is provided for customers that previously created peering/Route53 manually: 'redwood private-installer import-network-manifest' will adopt resources by ARNs and populate the manifest.

Rollout plan: merge to main, cut release branch for private-installer 1.7.0, staged rollout to internal customers, enable automatic rollback by default for first two weeks.

Risks and mitigations: network mistakes can be destructive; we added a dry-run mode and extra confirmation for cross-account peering creation. Tags and owner metadata make cleanup straightforward.

Related: Linear ENG-3482, INF-229. Linked support case SUP-4421.

review_comments: Rohan Patel (reviewer): Please ensure endpoint policies are scoped; avoid wildcard principals in KMS access. Also add a test that simulates peering already existing.
Ava Martinez (author): Addressed: added KMS policy artifacts and a terratest case that simulates existing peering by pre-creating the peering resource; pushed updates in commit d4a8b77.
Lina Chen (reviewer): Can we add an opt-out for Route53 creation for customers using a central DNS provider? Also requested clearer error messages from the rollback hook.
Ava Martinez (author): Added variable control_plane_route53_create = false and improved rollback hook logging + exit codes in commit e5b6a22.
Marcus White (approver): Ran staging validation, LGTM. Suggest follow-up to add GCP/Azure provider parity for private-installer later. Approved with minor nits.
CI system: terraform plan validated in CI; helm lint passed; one flaky terratest was re-run and passed.
release_notes:
- Private deployments: new Terraform module 'vpc-control-plane' to provision multi-AZ private subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering, and Route53 private hosted zones.
- Private-installer: automatic network manifest generation and upgrade/rollback hooks to reduce failed-deploy fallout.
- Helm chart: added values examples to map networking resources to control-plane components.
- Migration: 'redwood private-installer import-network-manifest' command to adopt pre-existing resources.
notes_for_ops: Dry-run mode available via --network-dry-run. For cross-account peering the operator must have ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection on the peer account or provide the peer connection ID. Tags: managed_by=redwood, cluster_id=<cluster> are required for automated cleanup.
testing_summary: Unit: terraform fmt/lint + terratest mocks; Integration: staged run in staging-net-03 that verified endpoints and Route53; CI: all checks passing after re-run.
changelog_section: Added: vpc-control-plane terraform module; Added: private-installer upgrade/rollback networking hooks; Changed: helm chart network values; Docs: networking guide and migration steps.
